title: Daniel 3: the fiery furnace
opening_question: Nebuchadnezzar set up an image of gold and commanded all to bow; three young men would not. What did they answer the king, who walked with them in the fire, and what does that ask of us?

steps.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar set up, and what were all the people commanded to do at the sound of the music?

facts.text: In Daniel 2:38 the king is told "Thou art this head of gold"; in Daniel 3:1 he "made an image of gold".
"image" is tselem, the same word as the great image of Daniel 2:31. Strong's: "an idolatrous figure".

steps.question: Who accused the Jews, what did they say about the three men, and what did the king ask them?
What did the three men answer, and what did they say if God did not deliver them?

facts.text: "deliver" is shezab. Strong's: "to leave that is (causatively) free".

steps.question: How hot was the furnace, what happened to the men who threw them in, and what did the king see in the fire?

facts.text: The translations differ in Daniel 3:25: the King James says "the Son of God"; the Ethiopian Canon and the Berean Standard Bible say "a son of the gods". The Aramaic is bar elahin; elah is "God" or "god" (Strong's H426).

steps.question: What could the fire not do to them, and whom did the king bless?

facts.text: Not "an hair of their head singed", and "the smell of fire" had not passed on them.

steps.question: Where else does Scripture speak of walking through fire, of faith that quenched the violence of fire, and of an image all must worship?

facts.text: Daniel 3:6: whoso falleth not down "shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace". Revelation 13:15: as many as would not worship the image of the beast "should be killed".
